title: PHP fragment cache and prefs cookie
context: Caches rendered HTML fragments on disk under /var/cache/fragments. Keys are arbitrary strings that may contain user input; entries expire after their TTL, given in seconds. Many requests run concurrently and a reader must never see a half-written entry. load_prefs() reads display preferences from the 'prefs' cookie, which the client controls.
code: public function set(string $key, string $html, int $ttl): void

expected.why: the TTL is in seconds but multiplied by 1000, so entries live 1000 times longer than intended
the file is written in place, so concurrent readers can read a truncated or half-written entry; write a temp file and rename() it
the raw key is used as a path, so "../" in a key reads or writes outside the cache directory; hash the key
unserialize on a client-controlled cookie allows PHP object injection; use json_decode
